system_type_reason: Library that plugs a tool-use layer into other agents (AnyTool.execute); not a standalone end-user agent.

repo_overview.summary: Universal tool-use layer that can be plugged into any agent. AnyTool.execute(task) hands the task to a single GroundingAgent, which first retrieves relevant tools across MCP, shell, GUI and web backends (embedding/keyword ranking plus an LLM filter) and then runs an iterative OpenAI-style function-calling loop until the model emits <COMPLETE> or the iteration cap is reached. A persistent tool-quality manager feeds execution statistics back into tool ranking across runs.

components.purpose: public AnyTool facade: wires LLM client, GroundingClient and agent, execute() entry point, periodic quality evolution
GroundingAgent: the iteration loop, message truncation, visual analysis of screenshots, workspace artifact check, final summary
LLMClient over litellm: rate limiting, call retry, in-call tool execution, tool-result summarization
GroundingClient (providers, sessions, invoke_tool), tool search/ranking, tool quality tracking, security policies and E2B sandbox, tool/session/transport base classes
tool backends: mcp (client, installer, tool cache, transport connectors), shell, gui (Anthropic computer-use client), web
Flask server for server mode, executing shell/GUI actions on a VM or remote machine; health and feature checkers, platform adapters
client side for screenshots, recording and system info
trajectory, action and video recording plus viewer
JSON configs (agents, grounding, security, mcp) and loader
system and helper prompts of the GroundingAgent
CLI entry point with live UI

topology.justification: Hierarchical boss and helper structure. The GroundingAgent (tool_layer.py:166) is the orchestrator: its LLM loop selects tools and delegates sub-tasks as a task description to the shell_agent and gui_agent tools. Each of these helpers is a separate LLM agent with its own system prompt, its own LLM client and its own multi-turn loop: shell_agent writes and runs code for up to 5 steps with execution feedback until TASK_COMPLETED or TASK_FAILED (shell/session.py:123, 263-334), gui_agent observes screenshots, plans and executes actions with its own Anthropic computer-use model for up to max_steps until DONE or FAIL (gui/tool.py:150-231). The helpers report back to the orchestrator as a ToolResult. The remaining LLM calls (LLM tool filter in search, tool-result summarization, visual analysis, deep research distillation) are single-shot helper calls and count as tools.

resilience.name: iteration cap with incomplete status
resilience.what_it_is: The GroundingAgent loop runs at most max_iterations rounds (15 in config_agents.json, fallback default 20 in AnyToolConfig, overridable per execute() call). Reaching the cap without <COMPLETE> returns status 'incomplete' with a warning and the last assistant message.
resilience.function_in_system: Outer bound of the agent loop in GroundingAgent.process(). Stops runs where the model never declares completion and caps LLM and tool cost per task, while still returning the partial result to the caller. Otherwise a model that keeps calling tools loops indefinitely.

resilience.name: per-iteration completion check nudge
resilience.what_it_is: After every iteration without <COMPLETE>, a system message 'Iteration N complete. Check if task is finished, if yes output <COMPLETE>' is appended; the nudge from the previous iteration is removed first so only one exists.
resilience.function_in_system: End of each iteration in GroundingAgent.process(), feeding into the next LLM call. resilience.name: LLM call retry with error-classified backoff and timeout
resilience.what_it_is: Every LLM call is wrapped in asyncio.wait_for with a 120s timeout and up to 3 attempts (llm_max_retries). Timeouts retry after 1s; rate-limit errors (429, 'rate limit') wait 60s + 30s per attempt to cross the rate-limit window; server overload errors (overloaded, 500-504) use exponential backoff 5s, 10s, 20s capped at 60s; all other errors are re-raised immediately.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps litellm.acompletion inside LLMClient.complete(), so it covers every agent turn and the tool-retrieval LLM. Absorbs transient provider failures and hung requests within a single iteration. Otherwise one rate-limit spike or stalled request aborts the whole task run.

resilience.name: tool failures returned to the model as error observations
resilience.what_it_is: Calls to unknown (hallucinated) tool names and exceptions during tool execution are converted into ToolResult(status=ERROR), rendered as an '[ERROR] ...' tool message and appended to the conversation; the loop continues. resilience.name: task-driven tool retrieval with layered fallback to the full tool list
resilience.what_it_is: When more tools are available than max_tools (40 in config_grounding.json), SearchCoordinator selects a task-relevant subset. Non-MCP tools (shell, gui, web) are always kept; only MCP tools are ranked. Above llm_filter_threshold (50) MCP tools an LLM drafts a brief plan and classifies servers into utility tools and domain servers, with the prompt instruction to include a server when in doubt; if the result still exceeds the limit, utility tools are kept and domain tools are ranked into a quota of max(max_tools - utility_count, 5). Below the threshold an LLM appends capability keywords to the query. Ranking is hybrid: BM25 preselects top_k*3, then cosine similarity of bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings re-ranks. A six-level fallback chain degrades step by step: LLM filter exception to direct ranking, unparsable or empty LLM filter result to all tools as domain, semantic search unavailable to keyword results, keyword search without matches to all tools, search exception to the first max_tools candidates, auto-search exception in GroundingAgent to the full tool list of all backends.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs before the first LLM call in GroundingAgent.process() and decides which tool schemas enter the prompt. Keeps prompt size and tool-choice noise bounded when many MCP servers are connected. The fallback chain guarantees a non-empty toolset whenever any retrieval step fails. Otherwise an embedding or LLM failure starts the agent without tools, or hundreds of tool schemas fill the context window.

resilience.name: failure-rate penalty in tool ranking from persisted execution history
resilience.what_it_is: Every tool call through BaseTool.arun records success and latency in a ToolQualityManager, which persists all records to .anytool/tool_quality/records.json after each execution (backup copy, version check on load), so the history carries over across sessions. A tool with at least 3 calls whose success rate over its last 100 executions falls below 0.4 gets a penalty factor 0.3 + (rate/0.4)*0.7, reduced by a further 0.1 per consecutive failure from the third one on (at most 0.3), clamped to [0.2, 1.0]. SearchCoordinator multiplies each selected MCP tool's score by this factor and re-sorts. The re-sort runs on the already truncated result list, so it reorders the tools shown to the model and removes tools only when the LLM filter quota exceeds max_tools. It runs only when tool retrieval is triggered (more than 40 tools). Exceptions caught by handle_errors in arun bypass the recording; failures returned as error ToolResults are counted.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the end of the tool retrieval step before the first LLM call and feeds on outcomes of earlier tool calls, including those of previous runs. Pushes repeatedly failing MCP tools to the back of the tool list the model sees. Otherwise a broken MCP server keeps the same prominence as a working one and the agent spends iterations on it.

resilience.name: command blocklist with interactive user confirmation for shell and Python execution
resilience.what_it_is: Before every bash script or Python code execution, both shell connectors (local subprocess mode and local_server mode) call SecurityPolicyManager.check_command_allowed. The policy merges the global and the shell backend policy from config_security.json and combines the common blocklist with the entries for the current OS (17 tokens on darwin, e.g. rm, -rf, dd, chmod, 777, passwd, killall). The command is split with shlex.split and blocked on any exact token match. On a match the CLI shows the detected tokens and affected lines and asks the user; only y/yes allows execution, and a prompt exception or EOF on stdin denies it. A denial raises PermissionError, which reaches the model as a tool error. Token matching misses nested commands (bash -c "rm -rf x" yields the single token 'rm -rf x') and Python file operations such as shutil.rmtree, matches harmless uses of tokens like root or 777, and code with an unbalanced quote (e.g. a comment containing don't) makes shlex.split raise ValueError inside check().
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model's shell tool call and execution on the host, which is the default setup (shell mode local, no sandbox). Holds destructive system commands for human approval and falls back to denial in headless runs. Otherwise a model-generated rm -rf or dd runs directly on the user's machine.

resilience.name: JSON-schema validation of tool arguments with error feedback
resilience.what_it_is: Before every tool execution BaseTool.arun validates the model-supplied arguments against the tool's JSON schema with jsonschema.validate. A schema violation raises GroundingError('Invalid parameters: <message>'), and arguments passed to a tool that declares no parameters raise ValueError. handle_errors (on by default) turns both into an error ToolResult carrying the concrete violation.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model's tool call and backend execution. Catches missing required fields and wrong types before any shell, MCP or GUI side effect happens and gives the model a specific, correctable error message. Otherwise malformed arguments reach the backend and fail there with unspecific errors or partial effects.
